content.text:
This `.gitignore` uses an allowlist strategy — `*` on line 13 ignores everything by default, then specific paths are un-ignored below (`.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md`, `settings.json`, `commands/`, `skills/`, `hooks/`, `agents/`, `rules/`).

`.agents` (with the dot) isn't on that allowlist — only `agents/` (no dot) is. So the skill installer put the systematic-debugging skill in a differently-named directory than what this repo's `.gitignore` expects, and it's getting swept up by the catch-all `*` rule.

content.text:
Confirmed: `.agents/skills/...` exists but there's no plain `agents/` directory — so the `!agents/` allowlist entry in `.gitignore` never matches anything real; this skill installer uses the dotted `.agents` convention instead. That's why it silently gets swallowed by the catch-all `*` ignore rule.

Want me to add allowlist entries for `.agents/` (and `.agents/**`) to `.gitignore` so these skills get committed and survive a clone to a new machine?
